text: Sigurd Arthur Aalefjær (14 September 1917 – 10 March 1991) was a Norwegian engineer, civil servant, and director of Norwegian hydropower plants. He was born in Bend, Oregon, as the son of Wilhelm Torjussen Aalefjær (1881–1969) and Inger Larsen Kostøl (1890–1975), and the family relocated to Vennesla in Vest-Agder, Norway. He married Magda Synnøve Berg (1920–2002) in 1943 and lived and died in Bærum. He completed his secondary education at Kristiansand Cathedral School in 1937 and earned a construction engineering degree from the Norwegian Institute of Technology in Trondheim in 1941. He worked for the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Agency from 1942 to 1946, then at Drammens Elektrisitetsverk from 1946 to 1949, and returned to the Water Resources and Energy Agency in 1949. From 1960 until his retirement in 1984, he served as the director of Statskraftverkene (now Statkraft). He was awarded the Knight, First Class of the Order of St. Olav in 1983.
